Ontology_AssayAndWorkflow_prompt.notes: The experiment uses Proteomics of Isolated Chromatin fragments (PICh), which is a specialized form of affinity purification (AP-MS) targeting a specific genomic locus using biotinylated probes and streptavidin beads. Acquisition on a Q Exactive HF without mention of DIA or targeted methods implies DDA. Quantification is label-free (LFQ) based on peptide intensities and NSAF.

scope: we applied a mass spectrometry-based approach to identify chromatin-bound proteins occupying the promoter region of CDKN1A
Each sample (corresponding to 24 million cells) was incubated with 6 pmol of either CDKN1A targeting (“F2”, GTAAACCTTAGCCTGTTACTCTGAACAGGGTATGTGATCTGCCAGCAGAT) or reversed, negative control probe
100 µL of streptavidin beads (New England Biolabs, Ipswich, MA, USA; pre-prepared by blocking for the MS experiment, as described in) was added to each of the tubes.
Affinity purification coupled with mass spectrometry proteomics
subcellular_fraction: The pellet, containing DNA with cross-linked proteins, was suspended in freshly-prepared 25 mM NaOH

Ontology_TreatmentAndDesign_prompt.notes: The proteomics experiment (PICh) specifically analyzes the chromatin-bound proteome of the CDKN1A promoter in p53KO cells treated with doxorubicin. While the paper extensively discusses ZNF84 siRNA knockdown, that perturbation was used for functional validation (RT-PCR, Western Blot, etc.) and not as the primary variable for the mass spectrometry run described in the PICh protocol.
